name: Ted Ellsworth
title: PhD
short_bio: Ted is the Manager of Yale's StatLab and holds a PhD in Government and Politics from the University of Maryland, College Park. His expertise spans causal inference, machine learning, natural language processing, and Bayesian methods.
bio: Ted Ellsworth is the manager of Yale's StatLab. Prior to coming to Yale, Ted received a PhD in Government and Politics from the University of Maryland, College Park.

name: Muji Chughtai
title: PhD Candidate
short_bio: Muji is a PhD Candidate in Psychology. His research specializes in emotions across social contexts, large-scale data analysis, and dimensionality reduction techniques.
bio: I am a PhD candidate in (social) psychology, and my research broadly focuses on emotions and how they vary across social contexts. Before becoming a PhD candidate, I received a B.S. in Psychology and a B.S. in Statistics from the Ohio State University and an M.A. in Statistics from Yale. I really enjoy using large-scale datasets to better understand complex phenomena (like human behavior), and I have taught mentees and students to do this through my teaching experiences in my graduate and undergraduate training. I am especially passionate about expanding theory by using methodological and analytical techniques that allow researchers to appreciate the inherent complexity of important outcomes. This often takes the form of using dimensionality reduction techniques, fitting multilevel models, and designing informative plots with multiple key predictor variables.

name: Kevin Jin
title: PhD Candidate
role: PhD Candidate · Computational Biology & Biomedical Informatics
short_bio: Kevin is a PhD Candidate in Computational Biology and Biomedical Informatics. His research specializes in large language models for psychiatric treatment recommendation, natural language processing, and causal inference.
bio: Hey! Thanks for checking out my profile. My research centers on training a large language model for evidence-grounded psychiatric treatment recommendation. I specialize in LLMs but have secondary interests in classical natural language processing, classical machine learning, causal inference, time series, model interpretability, and Bayesian reasoning. I love advising on types of analyses to perform, interpreting results, understanding models and coefficients, and learning more statistics in general! If you're not sure whether your project fits, just hit me up and let's chat — I'd love to see what I can do for you, and if I can't help you directly, I'll be sure to point you in the direction of someone who can.

name: Atalay Demiray
title: PhD Candidate
role: PhD Candidate · Health Policy and Management
short_bio: Atalay is a PhD Candidate in Health Policy and Management. His research specializes in decision-analytic modeling, applied health economics, and women's health and tobacco regulation.
bio: I'm a PhD candidate in Health Policy and Management (Economics Track) at Yale, where I use decision-analytic modeling, microsimulation, and applied health economics to study women's health, tobacco regulation, and chronic diseases. I do most of my modeling in R, with a particular interest in reproducible workflows, simulation methods, and cost-effectiveness analysis. Before Yale, I trained in medicine at Koç University and in health economics at Erasmus University Rotterdam, so clinical and healthcare research questions sit squarely in my area of expertise. I most enjoy helping researchers with study design, regression and survival analysis of health data, decision and simulation modeling, and translating clinical/policy questions into analysis.

name: Cole Brookson
title: PhD Candidate
short_bio: Cole is a PhD Candidate in Epidemiology (Microbial Diseases). His research specializes in climate change and infectious disease dynamics, statistical forecasting, and Bayesian methods.
bio: I am a PhD Candidate in the department of Epidemiology (Microbial Diseases), and I work on developing methods for understanding the impacts of climate and climate change on infectious disease dynamics, as well as the theory behind statistical forecasting. My background is in ecology and statistics/computation. While I enjoy supporting all of the interesting questions that come to the StatLab, I'm most knowledgeable about regression-based statistics. I have specific interests in Bayesian approaches, and simulation-based power analyses, as well as generally supporting work in the biological and health sciences.

name: Jonathan Elkobi
title: PhD Student
short_bio: Jonathan is a PhD Student in Political Science at Yale. His research focuses on elite politics and speech, local governments, and municipal bond markets, using text-as-data approaches with LLMs and NLP.
bio: I am a PhD student in the Department of Political Science at Yale. My research focuses on elite politics and elite speech, local governments, and politics and financial markets. Methodologically, I develop computational social science tools, especially text-as-data approaches using Large Language Models (LLMs) and Natural Language Processing (NLP), to measure political elite behavior and political speech. A major part of my research agenda examines municipal bond markets in the United States and China. I also work on side projects on other local-government economic outcomes, including pollution and growth, and on other markets such as prediction markets.

name: Claudia Mastrogiacomo
title: PhD Candidate
short_bio: Claudia is a Data Scientist and PhD Candidate in Biostatistics. Their research specializes in Bayesian causal inference for randomized experiments with interference and non-adherence, with applications in public health and criminal justice policy.
bio: I am a Data Scientist and PhD Candidate in Biostatistics. My research is in Bayesian causal inference, specifically in randomized experiments with interference and non-adherence. I am interested in applications in public health and criminal justice policy. I enjoy helping with choosing study designs and planning analyses to answer causal questions.

name: Prabaha Gangopadhyay
title: PhD Candidate
short_bio: Prabaha is a PhD Candidate in Psychology with a focus in neuroscience. Their research specializes in neural signals in the prefrontal cortex and amygdala during social communication in primates.
bio: I am a PhD candidate in the Department of Psychology at Yale, with a focus in neuroscience. My research asks how complex social behaviors are encoded in the brain: I record neural signals in the prefrontal cortex and amygdala while primates communicate and compete over resources, and ask what makes animals cooperate rather than compete. Before Yale I completed a four-year bachelor's degree and a one-year master's degree in biology at the Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore. Much of my day-to-day work is large-scale data management and cluster computing, and at the StatLab I most enjoyed helping with high-performance computing workflows, theoretical modeling and simulation, hypothesis testing, and machine learning.

name: Jiye Kwon
title: PhD
short_bio: Jiye completed a PhD in Epidemiology of Microbial Diseases at Yale in spring 2026. Their research specializes in pathogen genomics and the statistical and mathematical modeling of infectious diseases.
bio: I completed my PhD in the Department of Epidemiology of Microbial Diseases at Yale in spring 2026. My work sits at the intersection of pathogen genomics, bioinformatics, and mathematical modeling of infectious diseases — using sequence data alongside transmission models to inform intervention strategies for enteric and respiratory diseases, including vaccine evaluation for rotavirus, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV. Before my doctorate I earned an MPH in public health modeling at Yale and studied the respiratory and gastrointestinal microbiome with the Antibacterial Resistance Leadership Group. At the StatLab I wrote the guide on logit and probit models, and most enjoyed helping with regression and mixed-effects modeling, Bayesian and time-series approaches, and getting genomic and clinical data into shape for analysis.
